battle.theater: 魁北克市郊與聖勞倫斯河下游
battle.brief: 七年戰爭自一七五四年北美的俄亥俄河谷衝突起，到一七六三年《巴黎條約》落幕，是第一場真正全球性的戰爭。英軍以燧發滑膛步槍的線性齊射在魁北克市郊的亞伯拉罕平原上擊垮法軍，奪下整個法屬北美；同一件武器也出現在印度普拉西、普魯士歐陸與加勒比海的戰場上。

kit.name: 燧發槍
kit.history: 擊錘打火比火繩穩。線性列陣的射速和精度都靠它撐著。

countries: 七年戰爭是兩套跨洲體系的正面對撞，交戰方遍及歐洲、北美、印度、加勒比海與西屬菲律賓。英國一方以英王國陸軍與皇家海軍為骨架：陸軍骨幹是六十個營的步兵團，另有騎兵團、龍騎兵與海軍陸戰隊，海外戰線則靠殖民地省民兵與「王軍」——正規營與地方民兵混編的臨時建制；倫敦以國會撥款的「補助」把錢轉給歐洲盟國，用財政而非兵力決定歐陸格局。北美的英軍兵源是紐約、紐澤西、賓夕法尼亞、麻薩諸塞與維吉尼亞的省民兵，一七五五年布賴登率領的遠征軍只有六個營加民兵，共約二千一百人。法國一方是本國正規軍、殖民地民兵與原住民盟軍的混合體：加拿大有法屬第一團與第二團，路易斯安那有法籍營，印度有法屬印度公司的軍隊與本地雇兵，歐洲有法國陸軍主力，原住民方面則有易洛魁、肖尼、奧達瓦與特拉華等部落聯盟，在北美由蒙卡爾姆統籌。西班牙直到一七六二年才以「家族密約」加入英方陣營；奧地利、俄國、瑞典分別在不同年份加入法方聯盟；普魯士是英國以補助養著的受援方，同時是法國在歐陸的主要敵手。
countriesEn: The Seven Years' War was the head-on collision of two transcontinental systems, with belligerents spread across Europe, North America, India, the Caribbean and the Spanish Philippines. On the British side the frame was the army and the Royal Navy of the United Kingdom: the backbone of the army was sixty regiments of foot, with cavalry regiments, dragoons and naval marines besides, while the overseas war was carried by the provincial militias of the colonies and by the 'Royalist' formations, ad hoc mixes of regular companies and local men; London decided the shape of European politics with money rather than men, voting 'subsidies' in Parliament for its allies. British manpower in North America came from the provincial militias of New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Massachusetts and Virginia; the expedition under General Braddock in 1755 was six companies of foot and militia, some two thousand one hundred men in all. The French side was a mixture of the metropolitan army, colonial militias and native allies: Canada had the first and second French regiments, Louisiana had French companies, India had the troops of the French East India Company together with locally hired sepoys, Europe held the main body of the French army, and among the native allies were bands of Iroquois, Shawnee, Ottawa and Delaware, coordinated in North America by Montcalm. Spain did not enter until 1762, joining the British camp through the Family Compact; Austria, Russia and Sweden joined the French alliance in different years; and Prussia was the British client maintained by subsidy and at the same time France's principal enemy on the Continent.
people: 關鍵人物分佈在北美、歐洲與印度三個戰區。北美方面，維吉尼亞的青年軍官喬治·華盛頓一七五四年率志願軍進入俄亥俄河谷，在需要運河的小堡「必然堡」與法軍小隊交火，被迫簽署投降書；一七五五年他以少校副官身分在蒙諾加希拉河畔目睹英軍與省民兵崩潰，日後成為獨立戰爭的統帥。威廉·約翰遜在紐約依靠莫霍克盟友維持英方在內陸的影響，後任皇家印第安事務總監，是英國原住民政策的關鍵人物。英軍方面，布賴登中將在蒙諾加希拉重創，兩年後戰死於都柏林；福布斯上校一七五八年沿阿巴拉契亞山脈陸路奪取杜肯堡；詹姆斯·沃爾夫中校一七五九年率兵夜渡聖查爾斯河，在亞伯拉罕平原迫使蒙卡爾姆陣亡，自己亦中彈身亡，兵權由詹姆斯·穆雷接任；西蒙·弗雷澤上校在進攻卡里隆堡時陣亡。法國方面，路易-約瑟夫·德·蒙卡爾姆侯爵以少兵支撐廣大防線，是十八世紀最被低估的將領之一。歐洲方面，普魯士國王腓特烈二世獨力撐住歐陸；奧地利女皇瑪麗亞·特蕾莎的宮廷外交決定了同盟的生死；俄國女皇伊麗莎白在一七六〇年以「武裝中立」迫使法國接受和談；英國方面，威廉·皮特一七五七年出任首相，主持對普魯士的補助與全球封鎖。印度方面，羅伯特·克萊夫一七五七年於普拉西打敗孟加拉太守，赫克托·門羅一七六一年在布克薩爾擊敗莫臥兒聯軍，開啟了英國在印度的統治。
peopleEn: The decisive figures were spread across three theatres: North America, Europe and India. In North America the young Virginia officer George Washington led a volunteer force into the Ohio valley in 1754, fought a French detachment at the small stockade that had to be called Fort Necessity, and was forced to sign a surrender; in 1755 he was a major and aide-de-camp when he watched Braddock's army and the provincial militia collapse on the Monongahela, and he would one day command the American Revolution. William Johnson maintained British influence in the interior from New York through his Mohawk allies and later headed the Royal Indian Department, making him the key man of British native policy. On the British side Braddock was badly mauled at the Monongahela and died of his wounds in Dublin two years later; Colonel Forbes took Fort Duquesne in 1758 along the land route over the Appalachians; Lieutenant-Colonel James Wolfe crossed the St Charles by night in 1759, forced Montcalm to fall on the Plains of Abraham and was himself shot dead, the command passing to James Murray; Simon Fraser was killed leading his company in the attack on Fort Carillon. On the French side Louis-Joseph de Montcalm, Marquis de Montcalm, held an enormous front with a handful of men and is one of the most underrated commanders of the eighteenth century. In Europe Frederick II of Prussia bore the continental war almost alone; the court diplomacy of the Austrian empress Maria Theresa decided the life or death of the alliances; the Russian empress Elizabeth forced France to accept terms in 1760 through an armed neutrality; in Britain William Pitt became prime minister in 1757 and directed both the subsidy to Prussia and the global blockade. In India Robert Clive defeated the governor of Bengal at Plassey in 1757, and Hector Munro beat the Mughal army at Buxar in 1761, opening the way to British rule in India.
kits: 燧發滑膛步槍是英軍步兵的骨幹。制式武器是一七三二式「褐貝絲」燧發步槍：口徑標稱 .577 英寸（約十四點七毫米），槍管內膛平滑，槍口加厚以抗衝擊，配鉛彈與紙包定裝藥；士兵標準攜行量為六十發，另有通條、油壺與火繩盒。它不算精準，但便宜、易教，潮濕時仍可用火繩點燃。英軍在一七五九年以前完全沒有刺刀，直到魁北克之戰前夕才下令在突刺時裝上，一七八二年才列為制式配備。騎兵用燧發手槍與卡賓槍，炮兵用二磅、四磅、六磅與十二磅野戰炮。法軍使用一七一七年式王室步槍與一七五九年的夏萊維爾式步槍，後者以鋼件取代黃銅配件，射速比英軍慢，卻配更多火炮，每千人約六門，是當時歐洲最高的火砲密度。殖民地民兵與原住民用獵槍與自製的補丁長槍，精度遠勝制式滑膛槍但射速慢，在森林中特別有效。攻城靠臼砲、壕溝與艦上卸下的火炮；一七六二年英軍攻哈瓦那即以海軍陸戰隊配合可拆卸的速射炮與臼砲作戰。運輸依賴騾隊、大車與海運：一七五八年福布斯遠征軍帶了一千三百至一千五百輛大車，走四百餘英里，單線補給一斷全軍即停。主力艦每艘載砲五十至七十門，兵員四百至八百人，另有商船改裝的私掠船與載有登陸艇的運輸船隊。
kitsEn: The flintlock smoothbore musket was the backbone of the British infantry. The standard weapon was the 1732-pattern 'Brown Bess' flintlock musket: a nominal calibre of .577 inch, about 14.7 millimetres, with a smooth barrel, a muzzle reinforced against impact, and a lead ball carried in a paper cartridge; the standard soldier's burden was sixty rounds, together with the ramrod, the oil horn and the powder horn. It was not accurate, but it was cheap, easy to teach, and could still be fired with a match in wet weather. The British carried no bayonets at all before 1759; the order to fix them for the charge was issued on the eve of the battle of Quebec, and they did not become standard equipment until 1782. Cavalry used flintlock pistols and carbines, and the artillery used two-, four-, six- and twelve-pounder field guns. The French used the 1717-pattern royal musket and the Charleville musket of 1759, the latter replacing its brass fittings with steel; its rate of fire was slower than the British, but it carried more guns, roughly six field pieces per thousand men, the highest artillery density in Europe at the time. The colonial militias and the native allies used hunting guns and patched long arms of their own, far more accurate than the standard smoothbore but slow to fire and especially effective in the woods. Siege work was done with mortars, trenches and guns landed from ships; in 1762 the British assault on Havana used marine infantry together with dismountable swivel guns and mortars. Supply depended on mule trains, wagons and the sea: Forbes's expedition of 1758 took thirteen hundred to fifteen hundred wagons over more than four hundred miles, and a single break in that one-line supply stopped the whole army. A ship of the line carried fifty to seventy guns and four hundred to eight hundred men, and there were also converted merchantmen serving as privateers and transports with boats in their holds.
tactics: 戰術核心是十八世紀中葉的線性射擊。英軍以「一、二」號令分兩批齊射，步兵排成三排：第一排跪姿或舉槍齊射，第二排越肩而射，第三排裝填待命；理論上每分鐘可齊射四至五發，實戰常見每分鐘一至兩發。前裝單發的動作鏈是咬開紙包、傾藥、塞彈、捅通條、舉槍、擊錘打火，全套在幾十秒內完成，因此紙包的防潮、裝填速度與射手的訓練比射程更決定勝負。一七五五年蒙諾加希拉之敗並非英軍火力不足，而是省民兵拒絕列陣、戰車隊滯留後方、偵察不足。一七五九年亞伯拉罕平原上，英軍分兩縱隊同時進攻，一隊沿蒙莫蘭西河側捲上，一隊直取下城，炮擊三輪未命中後高地團以刺刀衝鋒打亂法軍左翼，整場戰鬥不到二十分鐘。同夜英軍在暴雨中橫渡聖查爾斯河，士兵只帶乾糧與火繩，渡河後沿陡坡攀上峭壁。海上英軍以封鎖與奪取基地為主：一七五九年霍克在基伯龍灣攔截法國入侵艦隊，切斷其跨海計劃；一七六二年以海軍陸戰隊與臼砲攻下哈瓦那與馬尼拉。歐洲方面，普魯士用縱隊迂回與斜擊，避免與奧軍正面耗費。
tacticsEn: The core of the tactics was the linear volley fire of the mid-eighteenth century. The British fired in two divisions on the command of 'one, two', the infantry drawn up in three ranks: the first kneeling or standing at the shoulder to fire, the second firing over their heads, the third loading and waiting; in theory four or five rounds could be fired in a minute, in practice one or two. The sequence of a single muzzleloaded shot was to bite the paper cartridge, pour the powder, push the ball, ram, present and strike the flint, the whole of it done in a matter of seconds, so that the waterproofing of the cartridge paper, the speed of loading and the drill of the musketeer decided the fight more than range did. The defeat at the Monongahela in 1755 was not a shortage of British firepower; it was the refusal of the provincial militia to form up, the wagon train left behind and the lack of reconnaissance. On the Plains of Abraham in 1759 the British attacked in two columns at once, one rolling up the Montmorency side and one driving straight at the Lower Town; after three volleys had missed, the Highlanders charged with bayonets and disordered the French left, and the whole action was over in less than twenty minutes. That same night the British crossed the St Charles in a pouring rain, the men carrying only their rations and their matches, and climbed the steep slope above the river. At sea the British worked by blockade and by seizing bases: in 1759 Hawke intercepted the French invasion fleet at Quiberon Bay and cut the cross-Channel plan; in 1762 marine infantry and mortars took Havana and Manila. In Europe Prussia used columns, turning movements and the oblique order, avoiding a frontal war of attrition with the Austrian army.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。英軍步兵團由戰前約六十個增至戰後近九十個，常備軍總兵力由七萬上下增至八萬五千以上；皇家海軍作戰艦艇由一七五六年的約一百三十五至一百五十艘增至一七六三年三百艘以上，水兵由約三萬九千人增至六萬五千至七萬人。北美方面，一七五四年英軍與省民兵合計約七千人；一七五五年蒙諾加希拉之戰英軍約二千一百人，傷亡約一千四百，其中陣亡五百至六百，法軍與原住民盟軍約五百至六百人，損失僅數十；一七五七年威廉亨利堡守軍約五百五十人，陣亡一百九十三人、被俘二百六十二人；一七五八年卡里隆堡與提康德加，英軍約一萬六千人、損失逾二千，法軍約一萬二千人、損失約三千九百；一七五九年魁北克，英軍約七千至九千人、損失約一千六百至一千九百，法軍約七千人、損失約三千至四千人，兩位主將均陣亡；一七六〇年向蒙利爾推進的三路英軍合計約一萬七千人。歐洲與海上方面，一七五九年明登之戰法軍損失約四千、被俘約二千，聯軍損失不足二千；一七五九年基伯龍灣，英軍三十九艘主力艦對法軍二十二至二十四艘，法軍三艘被俘、一艘焚毀，約四千人死傷被俘；一七六二年哈瓦那，英軍投入約二萬二千人，西班牙守軍約一萬人，損失約三千五百人，另沉四艘以上戰列艦與數千名海員。傷亡總數的估算分歧很大：北美戰線英軍作戰與非作戰死亡約六千至一萬人，法軍與加拿大民兵約一萬人上下；全戰線英軍死亡約二萬五千至五萬人，法軍約三萬至四萬人，差距主要來自疾病與俘虜的處理方式。財政上，英國國債由約五千萬鎊升至一七六四年的約一億四千萬鎊，利息支出由每年約二百五十萬鎊升到約四百五十萬鎊。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. British regiments of foot rose from about sixty at the outbreak to close to ninety by the end of the war, and the total strength of the regular army grew from some seventy thousand men to over eighty-five thousand; the Royal Navy's warships went from about one hundred and thirty-five to one hundred and fifty in 1756 to more than three hundred in 1763, and its sailors from about thirty-nine thousand to between sixty-five and seventy thousand. In North America the British and the provincial militia together numbered about seven thousand in 1754; at the Monongahela in 1755 the British had some two thousand one hundred men and lost about one thousand four hundred, of whom five to six hundred were killed, against five to six hundred French and native troops who lost only a few score; at Fort William Henry in 1757 a garrison of about five hundred and fifty lost one hundred and ninety-three dead and two hundred and sixty-two captured; at Carillon and Ticonderoga in 1758 sixteen thousand British lost more than two thousand, against twelve thousand French who lost about three thousand nine hundred; at Quebec in 1759 seven to nine thousand British lost about one thousand six hundred to one thousand nine hundred, and about seven thousand French lost three to four thousand, both commanders falling; in 1760 the three British columns converging on Montreal together numbered about seventeen thousand. In Europe and at sea, at Minden in 1759 the French lost about four thousand, some two thousand of them prisoners, against fewer than two thousand for the allies; at Quiberon Bay in 1759 thirty-nine British ships of the line met twenty-two to twenty-four French, three French ships being captured and one burnt, with about four thousand men killed, wounded or taken; at Havana in 1762 the British committed some twenty-two thousand men against a Spanish garrison of about ten thousand, which lost about three thousand five hundred, while more than four Spanish ships of the line and several thousand seamen went down. The estimates of total losses vary widely: in North America the British dead in action and from disease numbered about six to ten thousand, and the French and Canadian militia about ten thousand; across all theatres British dead are put at twenty-five to fifty thousand and the French at thirty to forty thousand, the gap coming mainly from disease and from how prisoners were treated. On finance, the British national debt rose from about fifty million pounds to roughly one hundred and forty million by 1764, and the interest burden went from some two and a half million pounds a year to about four and a half million.
cause: 起因分三層。歐洲層面，奧地利在《阿亨條約》之後一直謀求收復失去的西里西亞，普魯士則要守住這片富庶產地；一七五六年普魯士先攻入薩克森，歐洲大戰隨即開打。法國態度的轉折是史稱「外交革命」的一連串動作：一七五六年一月法奧結盟，五月《凡爾賽條約》把法國正式綁上奧地利一方；法國的算盤是拆散英普同盟、把英國的注意力從北美拉回歐洲，並趁普魯士被拖住時取回上次戰爭失去的萊茵地位。殖民地層面，英法在俄亥俄河谷與五大湖上游的推進幾乎正面相撞：法國一七五四年在河谷建起杜肯堡，英國一七五四年在必然堡受挫，一七五五年布賴登遠征慘敗，才逼英國改弦更張，改以聯絡原住民的「七年聯盟條款」重建內陸影響，並於一七六一年設立皇家印第安事務部。直接導火線落在個人層面：華盛頓越過阿勒格尼山脈的探險、必然堡的槍聲與那份投降書，把兩國的邊界爭議變成了流血衝突。
causeEn: The causes lay on three levels. On the European level Austria had been trying to recover Silesia since the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, while Prussia needed to keep that rich province; in 1756 Prussia struck first into Saxony and the great European war opened. The change in the French attitude came in a series of moves known as the Diplomatic Revolution: the Franco-Austrian alliance of January 1756, and the Treaty of Versailles of May 1756, which formally tied France to the Austrian side. French calculation was to break the Anglo-Prussian link, pull British attention back from North America to Europe, and recover the Rhine position lost in the previous war while Prussia was tied down. On the colonial level the British and French advances into the Ohio valley and the upper Great Lakes came into direct collision: France built Fort Duquesne in the valley in 1754, Britain was checked at Fort Necessity in the same year, and the wreck of Braddock's expedition in 1755 forced Britain to change course, rebuilding its influence in the interior through the 'Covenant Chain' of the Seven Nations and establishing the Royal Indian Department in 1761. The immediate spark lay on the personal level: Washington's crossing of the Alleghenies, the shots at Fort Necessity and the surrender paper signed there turned a boundary dispute between two states into a shooting war.
impact: 影響是重塑了世界秩序。第一，英國取得制海權與全球霸權：海軍規模三年間翻倍，殖民地從北美延伸到印度，公司在孟加拉取得「迪瓦尼」後，十八世紀末的印度收入成為英國財政的重要支柱，也讓英國海軍第一次能在大西洋、印度洋與太平洋同時巡弋。第二，英國被債務拖垮：國債由五千萬鎊升至一億四千萬鎊，利息支出翻近一倍，於是有了印花稅、湯森諸法與茶稅，也有了把北美殖民地推向革命的稅制。一七六三年的皇家公告把阿巴拉契亞山脈以西劃為原住民保留地、禁止英人屯田，卻又把原住民的處置權收歸王室，龐蒂亞克聯盟一七六三至一七六六年的戰爭正是這一轉折的直接產物，也種下往後賓夕法尼亞與俄亥俄河谷緊張的種子。第三，法國幾乎失去全部海外殖民地，財政逼近破產，被迫在此後進行海軍與財政改革，並在歐洲事務上退守。第四，普魯士保住西里西亞，取得歐洲三強之首的地位，此後參與瓜分波蘭；俄國借一七六二年的和約取得東普魯士，在波羅的海立足；奧地利靠瑪麗亞·特蕾莎的改革延續國運；西班牙在一七六二年參戰後獲得路易斯安那與新奧良，版圖達到頂點，卻在關鍵時刻被英國反噬。第五，七年戰爭是第一場真正全球性的戰爭，其後的英荷戰爭、美國獨立戰爭與拿破崙戰爭，都建立在它確立的海上秩序之上。
impactEn: The effects amounted to a reordering of the world. First, Britain gained command of the sea and a global hegemony: the navy doubled in size within three years, the colonies reached from North America to India, and after the company obtained the 'diwani' of Bengal the revenue of India in the late eighteenth century became a pillar of British finance, while the British navy could for the first time patrol the Atlantic, the Indian Ocean and the Pacific at once. Second, the war dragged Britain into debt: the national debt went from fifty million pounds to one hundred and forty million, the interest burden nearly doubled, and there followed the stamp duty, the Townshend Acts and the tax on tea, and with them a taxation system that pushed the North American colonies towards revolution. The Royal Proclamation of 1763 reserved the country west of the Appalachians for the natives and forbade British settlement, yet it also brought the disposal of the natives into royal hands, and the war of the Pontiac confederacy from 1763 to 1766 was the direct product of that turn; it planted the seeds of the later tension in Pennsylvania and the Ohio valley. Third, France lost almost all of its overseas possessions, its finances approached bankruptcy, it was forced into naval and fiscal reform, and it withdrew from the conduct of European affairs. Fourth, Prussia kept Silesia and took its place as the first of the three great powers of Europe, and would later join in the partition of Poland; Russia obtained East Prussia in the peace of 1762 and established itself on the Baltic; Austria prolonged the life of the Habsburg state through the reforms of Maria Theresa; Spain entered in 1762 and gained Louisiana and New Orleans, the greatest extent of its empire, only to be struck down by Britain at the critical moment. Fifth, the Seven Years' War was the first truly global war, and the Anglo-Dutch wars, the American Revolution and the Napoleonic wars that followed all rest on the maritime order it established.
result: 結果是英國在海上與殖民地得勝、法國失去全球霸權、普魯士保住西里西亞，而西班牙在關鍵時刻反遭重創。一七六三年二月十日《巴黎條約》簽訂：法國割讓加拿大與密西西比河以東的全部北美領土，把路易斯安那與新奧良讓給西班牙，把佛羅里達交給英國，只保留聖皮耶與米克隆、塞內加爾的幾個據點以及印度的幾處商站；英國取得北美、格林納達、多巴哥、聖露西亞、聖文森與多米尼克，並在印度取得對孟加拉的實際統治權，一七六五年再拿到「迪瓦尼」，把公司統治擴成直接統治；西班牙取得路易斯安那、新奧良與密西西比河流域，換回梅諾卡，卻失去了哈瓦那與馬尼拉；葡萄牙在南美洲的邊界亦因此擴張。普魯士在同年《于貝爾圖斯堡條約》保住西里西亞，歐洲戰場因此以「保住原狀」收場。海上，皇家海軍完成了對法國的封鎖，法國海軍在隨後十年裡重建；英軍在北美留下的堡壘與「原住民保留地」政策重塑了整個大陸的權力格局。戰爭沒有在歐洲造成任何一方的決定性戰場勝負，卻決定了接下來一百年世界的走向：法國退守歐洲本土，英國接管海洋、印度的航線與北美大陸，歐洲大陸則進入腓特烈二世所開啟的均勢時代。
resultEn: The result was a British victory at sea and in the colonies, the loss of the world hegemony by France, the retention of Silesia by Prussia, and a severe blow to Spain at the very moment it had entered the war. The Treaty of Paris was signed on 10 February 1763: France ceded Canada and all its North American territory east of the Mississippi, handed Louisiana and New Orleans to Spain and Florida to Britain, keeping only Saint Pierre and Miquelon, a few posts in Senegal and a handful of trading stations in India; Britain took North America, Grenada, Tobago, St Lucia, St Vincent and Dominica, and gained effective control over Bengal in India, obtaining the 'diwani' in 1765 and turning company rule into direct rule; Spain received Louisiana, New Orleans and the Mississippi valley, got Minorca back, and lost Havana and Manila; the Portuguese frontier in South America was also enlarged. Prussia kept Silesia in the Treaty of Hubertusburg of the same year, so that the European theatre closed with everything as it had been. At sea the Royal Navy completed the blockade of France, and the French navy rebuilt itself over the following ten years; the forts the British left in North America and the 'Indian reserve' policy reshaped the whole power structure of the continent. The war produced no decisive battlefield verdict for anyone in Europe, yet it decided the shape of the world for the following century: France withdrew into Europe proper, Britain took the oceans, the sea lanes of India and the North American mainland, and the European continent entered the balance-of-power era opened by Frederick II.
